quizzes.title: BAFTA Awards 2026: practice
quizzes.passage:
The British Academy of Film and Television Arts, known by the short form BAFTA, is the body that presents the awards bearing its name. The awards honour achievement in film and television, and each ceremony recognises people whose work has been judged best in the relevant year. The booklet entry is written as a reference, giving the winners under separate headings rather than telling a single story.

The most recent ceremony covered in the booklet is the 2026 edition. It handed out awards for the top film prize, for direction, and for lead performances by actors and actresses, and the booklet lists the winners for each of these honours. Other winners from the same ceremony are gathered in the same list.

Indian films and performers also feature in the entry. The booklet describes a history of Indian recognition at the awards, with some wins coming from decades earlier and others from more recent years. Each milestone is presented as a separate point that names a person or film, the award won, and the year of that award.

The entry gives the organisation's context in a few short points. Its honours are split across several areas of screen work, and these points sit alongside the list of winners. Together they cover both the body itself and the awards it gives out.

questions.q: In which year was BAFTA established?
questions.explanation: The booklet gives 1947 as the year BAFTA was established.

questions.q: In which city is BAFTA based?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists London, in the United Kingdom, as BAFTA's base.

questions.q: Which Indian actor became the first Indian to win a competitive BAFTA, in the Best Supporting Actress category?
questions.explanation: The booklet credits Rohini Hattangadi with this win for her role in Gandhi (1983).

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Boong became the first Indian film to win Best Children's and Family Film at the 2026 BAFTA Awards.
Reason (R): Boong is a Manipuri film directed by Lakshmipriya Devi.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements appear in the booklet, but the director detail does not explain why the film won.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Best Film
II. Best Director
III. Outstanding British Film
IV. Best Leading Actress
A. Jessie Buckley
B. Hamnet
C. Paul Thomas Anderson
D. One Battle After Another
questions.explanation: The booklet pairs One Battle After Another with Best Film, Paul Thomas Anderson with Best Director, Hamnet with Outstanding British Film and Jessie Buckley with Best Leading Actress.

questions.q:
Statements:
I. BAFTA is presented annually.
II. BAFTA's categories cover Games and Children's & Family Content.
III. Hamnet won Best Film at the 2026 BAFTA Awards.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, while III is wrong because Best Film went to One Battle After Another.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements about BAFTA awards are correct?
I. Asif Kapadia won Best British Film for The Warrior (2002).
II. A.R. Rahman won Best Film Music for Slumdog Millionaire (2009).
III. Rohini Hattangadi won Best Leading Actress for Gandhi (1983).
questions.explanation: Statement III is wrong because Hattangadi's award was for Best Supporting Actress, not Best Leading Actress.

quizzes.title: BAFTA Awards: short-answer practice
quizzes.passage:
The British Academy of Film and Television Arts is the organisation that presents the BAFTA awards. Its honours cover film and television work, and the booklet entry on the subject is set out as a short reference rather than as a long article. The entry deals with a recent ceremony and with a set of earlier milestones connected with Indian work. The subject is part of the Miscellaneous section of the booklet.

The recent ceremony is the 2026 edition. Its results are listed by category, and the top film prize, the director's award and the lead acting awards are among the honours shown. The booklet records each winner's name against the honour, so a reader can check the result for every category shown.

The milestones are recorded in separate points. One point describes a film from India that won a children's and family honour at the awards, and it names the director and the producers. Another point describes the first Indian performer to take a competitive acting honour, and it names the film for which the award was given.

A further point covers a British film honour given in an earlier year, and another covers an award for film music. The page also carries the publisher's website and the page numbers.

questions.q: In which year was BAFTA established? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet gives 1947 as the year BAFTA was established.

questions.q: Which film won Best Film at the 2026 BAFTA Awards? (title)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists One Battle After Another as the Best Film winner at the 2026 awards.

questions.q: Who won Best Leading Actress at the 2026 BAFTA Awards for Hamnet? (name)
questions.explanation: The booklet credits Jessie Buckley with Best Leading Actress for Hamnet.

questions.q: Which Manipuri film became the first Indian film to win Best Children's and Family Film at the 2026 BAFTA Awards? (title)
questions.explanation: The booklet records Boong as the first Indian film to win this award.

questions.q: Who directed the Manipuri film Boong? (name)
questions.explanation: The booklet names Lakshmipriya Devi as the director of Boong.

questions.q: In which film did Rohini Hattangadi win the Best Supporting Actress award at BAFTA? (film)
questions.explanation: The booklet says Hattangadi won this award for her role as Kasturba Gandhi in Gandhi, released in 1983.

questions.q: Which film earned A.R. Rahman a BAFTA for Best Film Music? (title)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists Rahman's Best Film Music award as being for Slumdog Millionaire in 2009.

quizzes.title: ASMITA Initiative: practice
quizzes.passage:
ASMITA is an initiative in the sports sector, and the booklet's entry on it sits in the Miscellaneous section of the March 2026 Current Affairs booklet. The name is an acronym. Its letters stand for Achieving Sports Milestone by Inspiring Women Through Action, a phrase that signals the initiative's focus on women in sport. The initiative is presented in the booklet as a single entry.

The entry is short and is arranged under a few headings. These headings cover the basic facts about the initiative: when it began, the body that runs it, the name it carried before the current name, and the goals it sets out. Each heading is a separate point, so the entry works as a summary rather than a narrative.

The goals are described in two parts. The first part concerns the level at which the initiative works, and the second concerns the type of talent it looks for. Both parts appear together in the entry, so a reader sees the aims of the initiative in one place.

The entry sits alongside other items in the same section of the booklet. Those items include award-related entries, and the section as a whole covers a mix of topics under the Miscellaneous heading. The entry appears on the same page as the Oscars material.

questions.q: In which year was ASMITA launched?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that ASMITA was launched in 2021.

questions.q: What was ASMITA earlier known as?
questions.explanation: The booklet notes that ASMITA was earlier known as Khelo India Women's League.

questions.q: Which ministry launched ASMITA?
options: Ministry of Women and Child Development
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
questions.explanation: The booklet says ASMITA was launched by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): ASMITA seeks to identify and nurture young sporting talent, especially from rural and tribal areas.
Reason (R): ASMITA seeks to promote sports participation among girls and women at the grassroots level.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both are listed objectives in the booklet, and neither one explains the other.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Launch year
II. Launching body
III. Earlier name
IV. Focus of talent search
A. Khelo India Women's League
B. 2021
C. Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
D. Rural and tribal areas
questions.explanation: The booklet gives 2021 as the launch year, the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports as the launching body, Khelo India Women's League as the earlier name, and rural and tribal areas as the focus of talent search.

questions.q:
Statements:
I. ASMITA was launched in 2021.
II. ASMITA was earlier known as Khelo India Women's League.
III. ASMITA's objectives do not include sports participation for women.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, while III contradicts the stated objective of promoting participation among girls and women.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements about ASMITA are correct?
I. ASMITA was launched in 2021.
II. ASMITA's objectives include identifying young talent from rural and tribal areas.
III. ASMITA was earlier known as Khelo India Men's League.
questions.explanation: Statement III is wrong because the earlier name was Khelo India Women's League.
